title: Is the test a good test?
text: But yeah, I, I guess I was just thinking about the, the way that the AI tests are stored and rendered and, you know, how many different models they've been applied to. And really the, the weighting of the test, it's, it's sort of like, a, is the test a good test? Um, if you can get a fairly like, okay, so it's sort of like the variance in the completion rate. If the completion rate is, you know, close to one, then it might not be the best test. You're only going to weed out the a small minority of, of the worst models that fail the test. If the completion rate is near zero, then it's just a bad test. It's like nobody's figuring it out. This is somebody messed up the architecture of this test. If the completion rate is anywhere in that kind of... not zero and not a hundred percent range then maybe there's some legitimacy to the test and i would say i i wouldn't i wouldn't necessarily say a 50 percent completion rate is like the optimal test but it is sort of like a very indicative like okay there's something going on here if 50 percent of models pass this test and 50 percent of models fail this test still it could be an indicator of a bad test maybe the models that are failing aren't actually failing that badly The criteria is just a little bit, you know, strict. And so they did something that was slightly incomplete, mostly correct, but being judged as incorrect based on the, the scoring criteria. So we don't, we want to avoid that. And I'm not sure how to do that, but you'll figure it out. Um, yeah.

keys: Define test quality by completion-rate variance across models
Near-100% completion rate means test too easy
Near-0% completion rate means test is broken
Mid-range completion rate suggests a legitimate, discriminating test
50% pass rate isn't necessarily optimal but is indicative
Avoid penalizing near-correct answers for overly strict criteria
Distinguish truly failing models from ones marked wrong unfairly
Figure out how to loosen/calibrate scoring criteria
Score each test by how well it separates models
Near-100% pass rate: weak test, catches only worst models
Near-0% pass rate: broken test, fix its design
Mid-range pass rate suggests a legitimate test
